newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up on dollar sales by banks.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up on dollar sales by banks.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended higher against the dollar on Wednesday as banks sold dollars to clear their long positions, dealers said.
The rupee ended at 35.645/655 per dollar against the day's opening 35.67/68, they said. The rupee traded at a high of 35.645 and a low fo 35.68 during the day, they said.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India bought dollars in small amounts late in the day at 35.65 rupees.

Premia on forward dollars opened lower from Tuesday's levels and fell further on expectations of improved domestic liquidity, dealers said. "Premia recovered to some extent on paying pressure late in the day but still ended below Tuesday's levels," a dealer said.
The premia for six-month dollars closed at 9.42 percent annualised against Tuesday's close of 9.52 percent, dealers said.
